newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates dip, Feb DTCs sold out.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates dip, Feb DTCs sold out.

text.p: Dutch one- to three month deposit rates eased a few basis points on Tuesday but dealers said the easing was too small to be described as a trend.

One month deposits were quoted at 2.97 to 2.98 percent bid, while three month deposits were bid between 2.99 and 3.02 percent, both some two basis points lower than on Monday. Call money was most active but was unchanged at 2.87/93.
Dealers said they did not expect any substantial moves in Dutch money market rates before the announcement of a Dutch government bond issue on January 17.
Dutch treasury certificates (DTCs) issued under the programme maturing on February 28 reached the maximum amount of 7.5 billion guilders today.
DTCs from the 7.5-billion-guilder programme maturing on March 27 were also said to be selling well, benefitting from a slightly weaker German mark versus the guilder, dealers said.
DTCs are short-term securities issued by the Dutch government on a discount-to-face-value basis.
Under EMU-linked policy changes announced last year the Dutch government and the Dutch central bank have agreed to make greater use of DTCs as a money market instrument from 1997.
The maximum amount of oustanding DTCs at any time has now been doubled to 30 billion guilders.
In addition to this, the Finance Ministry's debt agency will play a more active role in the money market.

A spokesman said that in view of this more active role the agency no longer planned to provide weekly updates of the outstanding amounts issued under the various DTC programmes and was reviewing what information it would disclose in future.
"The market knows what is going on (in DTCs). We are reshuffling our (information) pages, but I don't think we will put DTC-figures on the screens in the near future," he said.
The agency has a series of pages on the Reuter news system starting on page AGFB.
The guilder was quoted at 112.198 against 100 marks versus 112.240 yesterday.
